determinism.finding: The renderer is NOT frame-deterministic with depth of field enabled. Three consecutive G.render() calls on a frozen scene differ from each other by 2700-5300 pixels, max channel-sum 10-12, out of 960000.
determinism.isolatedBy: Turning each post effect off in turn. fx.ao/bloom/rays off still differ; fx.dof=0 alone gives 0 differing pixels.
determinism.consequence: THREEJS-MIGRATION.md section 5 asks for pixel A/B against previous-stage stills, and Stage 1 for bit-identical. That is unachievable as written unless DOF is off.
determinism.recipe: Set Game.fxSettings.dof = 0 before every comparison capture and restore afterwards. With DOF off the frame is bit-exact and A/B is meaningful.
determinism.note: This is also a live bug in its own right: a paused game shimmers. Not fixed here - out of scope for the migration - but worth an entry in BUGS.md.

stage1.what: three.js r180 adopted on the existing canvas and context; renders nothing.
stage1.whyR180: r169 has no THREE.ExternalTexture, which the brief's Stage 2 needs to let a three material sample the still-raw sceneFB. It lands in r180.
stage1.verification: Same JS task, identical frozen scene, dof off, R.three present vs null: 0 differing pixels of 960000.

resetStateWritesGlState.finding: three.resetState() in r180 does not only reset three's CACHE, it writes GL state to three's defaults. Measured at frameStart: depthMask false->true, blend dst ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA->ZERO, current program->null, clearColor (0,0,0,1)->(0,0,0,0).
resetStateWritesGlState.impact: With three merely adopted and drawing nothing, the frame changed by 222547 pixels of 960000. Pinning the clear colour around resetState brought it to exactly 0.
resetStateWritesGlState.cause: The renderer sets a clear colour before the scene clear but inherits the ambient one elsewhere, so it had always relied on nobody else touching it.
resetStateWritesGlState.fix: renderer.js threeResync() wraps resetState and restores gl.clearColor(0,0,0,1). One place, so a later stage cannot reintroduce it by adding a resetState call.
resetStateWritesGlState.briefGap: THREEJS-MIGRATION.md L14 warns that raw GL desyncs three's cache. The reverse - resetState moving real GL state under the hand-written passes - is not mentioned and is what actually bit.

statsCaveat: H.stats() draws/instances/tris scale with how much colony there is, not with the renderer. They ran 38/666/92556 at 4000 frames and 44/714/129646 at 5500. Compare them only at the same simulation age; the bit-identical pixel A/B is the real gate.

vendoring.note: r17x+ splits the browser build into three.core.min.js plus three.module.min.js, which imports from core AND re-exports it with an export{...}from"..." statement. Both forms have to be handled or the wrapper does not parse.
